prompt: Make the hero section of a landing page for Fernwick, a small tool that sends polite automatic reminders when a freelancer's invoices go unpaid. I want a headline, a short paragraph under it, a main button to start a free trial, a quieter link for a demo, and some kind of product visual built with HTML and CSS. It should feel like a real startup site.
prompt_suffix: Return the result as a single self-contained HTML file: all CSS inline, no external requests, system fonts only. Reply with one ```html fenced block and nothing else.
rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.
featuring_rule: Declared before any run: rank the 3 without-skill runs and the 3 with-skill runs separately by the blind judge's rubric mean (two passes with the sides swapped, scores averaged), and feature the median run of each arm. The best run is never chosen. The contact sheet shows all six runs.

pairs.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): The two heroes share almost the same headline, paragraph and layout, so the decision comes down to the calls to action and the product visual. A has a dark 'Start free' button in the nav that competes with the main free-trial button, and its dashboard (stats row, toast and email overlay) is busier and pulls attention from the headline. B has a single primary button and a calmer invoice list with an email card, but that card awkwardly covers row amounts and due dates. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A has one clear primary CTA. B's dark 'Start free' button in the nav competes with the hero button, and B's busier dashboard, with stats, a toast and a card spilling toward the copy, pulls more attention from the headline. B's visual is richer and more polished, but A's email popover clips the amount and status in one row, which looks a little unfinished. Even so, A follows the hierarchy goals more closely.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both heroes share a strong structure, with a large headline, one green primary button, a 14-day trial note and an invoice dashboard mockup. B wins because its visual is cleaner. In A, the tilted email card covers part of one invoice row and the name on the next, which looks messy, and A's bold black 'Watch a demo' link with a play icon competes with the button more than B's quiet underlined grey link. A's serif-italic headline has more personality, but B's left edges line up more neatly and its email and 'opened your reminder' toast tell the product story without clutter. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both heroes are polished and similar in structure. A keeps a cleaner hierarchy: its demo link is a light underlined text link that is clearly quieter than the button, and its invoice card with the email preview is specific to the product and stays calm. In B, the bold 'Watch a demo' with its play icon and the pill-shaped 'Sign in' button pull more attention, and the tilted email card hides invoice rows, which makes the visual busier and more likely to compete with the headline.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B's product visual is clean and fully contained: an invoice list, a reminder email preview and a 'paid' toast, all clearly about invoice reminders, with no truncation. A has a strong headline and good copy, but its visual runs off the right edge of the page. Names are truncated ('North Ha...', 'Meridian ...'), and the toast and email card are clipped, which makes it look broken. A also has a dark 'Start free' button in the nav that slightly competes with the main call to action. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is a clean, well-balanced hero: the headline clearly dominates, there's one strong button with a quieter underlined demo link, and the invoice list with a reminder email preview fits the product while sitting fully inside the frame. B's visual is clipped off the right and bottom edges, with truncated names, cramped wrapping and a cut-off toast. B's dark 'Start free' nav button also competes with the hero CTA, and its bold demo link is less clearly secondary.
